title: Expanding Brackets
page_title: Expanding Brackets | Cambridge (CIE) A Level Maths Revision Notes 2021

blocks.md: You should be familiar with all aspects of basic algebra including manipulating expressions; simplifying; expanding and factorising brackets with both linear and quadratics.  In Pure Mathematics it is important that you are confident working with quadratics.

blocks.text: How do I expand two brackets?

blocks.md:
- You will have learnt a method for expanding double brackets in previous courses

  - The quickest and most common method is to use **FOIL**
  
    - **First** term in each bracket
    - **Outside** terms
    - **Inside** terms
    - **Last** terms
  - For (*ax* + *b*)(*cx* + *d*) you will have *acx*<sup>2 </sup>+ *adx* + *bcx* + *bd*
- Once you have expanded and multiplied all four terms simplify the two middle terms to give you a three-term quadratic

  - *acx*<sup>2 </sup>+ (*ad* + *bc*)x + *bd*
- Take extra care when working with negatives
- Look out for a linear expression squared, this must still be treated as double brackets

  - (*ax* + *b*)<sup>2 </sup>= *a*<sup>2</sup>*x*<sup>2 </sup>+ 2*abx* + *b*<sup>2</sup>
- Makes sure you can recognise when a problem involves the **difference of two squares**

  - (*ax* + *b*)(*ax* – *b*)<sup> </sup>= *a*<sup>2</sup>*x*<sup>2 </sup>+ *abx* - *abx* - *b*<sup>2 </sup>= *a*<sup>2</sup>*x*<sup>2 </sup>- *b*<sup>2</sup>
  - Spotting this will be particularly useful in many areas of Pure Mathematics

blocks.text: How do I expand brackets with quadratic terms?

blocks.md:
- Treat these the same as expanding double brackets with two linear expressions
- Take care with powers, remember the laws of indices
- Look carefully to see if the terms can be simplified or not

  - For (*ax*<sup>2</sup> + *b*)(*cx*<sup>2</sup> + *d*) you will have *acx*<sup>4 </sup>+ *adx*<sup>2</sup> + *bcx*<sup>2</sup> + *bd* = *acx*<sup>4 </sup>+ (*ad* + *bc*)x<sup>2</sup> + *bd*
  - For (*ax*<sup>2</sup> + *b*)(*cx* + *d*) you will have *acx*<sup>3 </sup>+ *adx*<sup>2</sup> + *bcx* + *bd*

blocks.text: How do I expand brackets with more than two terms?

blocks.md: - To expand brackets, the rule is that each term in one set of brackets must be multiplied by each term in the other set of brackets

blocks.alt: 2.5.1 Expanding Brackets Illustration, Edexcel A Level Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md:
- 'FOIL' is a special case of this, when each set of brackets contains two terms
- If you are trying to expand something like **(*****a***** + *****b*****)**<sup>***n***</sup>** **for powers of ***n*** greater than 2 or 3, use the **binomial expansion**
- If you have to expand more than two sets of brackets, just expand them two at a time:
